supporting_observations.claim: The alerted HTTPS checks are associated with C:\Program Files\RouteWise\routewiseupd.exe: the process started shortly before the 13:41 check, and its network event connects to the proxy at the same time.

The proxy records show repeated CONNECT requests from WS-KNGUYEN-01 to update.routewise.com from 13:41 through 14:10, at intervals broadly consistent with the inventoried RouteWise updater's approximately five-minute update checks.

For several of those checks, process-level network events identify routewiseupd.exe connecting to the proxy, corroborating that the periodic destination matches the approved updater rather than merely sharing a timestamp with an unrelated browser connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records establish CONNECT destinations and connection metadata, but the evidence does not show the contents of the RouteWise HTTPS sessions.
The supplied process records identify the RouteWise executable by path and name, but do not establish its file hash, signature, or integrity.
claims_not_established: The exact data exchanged or any changes made by the updater during its HTTPS sessions.
Whether the scheduled svc-routes password rotation had any operational effect on the separate RouteSync job; the evidence does not link that job or rotation to the alerted workstation traffic.
unrelated_findings: Review separately whether kim.nguyen's access to customer.cloud.com/Citrix/StoreWeb is approved; proxy records show the portal request and related page resources, but do not establish what the user did there. This does not determine the RouteWise alert disposition. (T126-00160, T126-00161, T126-00169, T126-00170, T126-00172)

A network logon for kim.nguyen to WS-KNGUYEN-01 is recorded from WS-DREYES-01 using NTLM. Investigate separately; the records do not establish its purpose or connection to the alerted HTTPS checks. (T126-00213, T126-00214)

WS-KNGUYEN-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-COP-01, where an ANONYMOUS LOGON network session was recorded. Review separately; this is not evidence about the alerted RouteWise HTTPS activity. (T126-00291, T126-00292, T126-00293, T126-00295)

kim.nguyen launched PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass to run C:\Scripts\backup-check.ps1. The supplied records do not establish the script's contents or whether it is authorized; review separately, without using it to decide this alert. (T126-00189, T126-00190)
